# Reference rules

A document written for the side reader's suite. Its shape is the shape a citation has to survive:
enumerated headings at more than one depth, a heading with no enumerator, two headings that say
the same thing, a fenced block with a hash inside it, a table, and a list.

## 1. The first rule

The first rule is stated here, and it has no subsections.

## 2. The second rule

The second rule has two of them.

### 2.1 The nearer half

Its text sits under a third-level heading, and the citation that names it should land here.

### 2.2 The further half

And this one under another.

## A rule with no number in front of it

Some headings carry no enumerator, and a section index has to list them just the same.

### Detail

One of two headings that say exactly the same word.

### Detail

The other one. A citation that names it can only be answered with "more than one".

## 3. Shapes this reader has to survive

```
# This hash opens no section: it is inside a fence, and a fence is code.
value = 1
```

| Column | What it holds |
|---|---|
| Left | A cell |
| Right | Another cell |
